To convert $\sqrt{2} e^{11 \pi i/4}$ to rectangular form, we use Euler's formula:
\[ e^{11 \pi i/4} = \cos(11 \pi/4) + i \sin(11 \pi/4) \]
\[ \cos(11 \pi/4) = \cos(3 \pi/4) = -\sqrt{2}/2 \]
\[ \sin(11 \pi/4) = \sin(3 \pi/4) = -\sqrt{2}/2 \]
Thus,
\[ e^{11 \pi i/4} = -\sqrt{2}/2 - i \sqrt{2}/2 \]
Multiplying by $\sqrt{2}$:
\[ \sqrt{2} e^{11 \pi i/4} = -\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{2}/2 - i \sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{2}/2 \]
\[ = -1 - i \]
So, the rectangular form of $\sqrt{2} e^{11 \pi i/4}$ is:
\[
\boxed{-1 - i}
\]

grade.gold_answer: We have that $\sqrt{2} e^{11 \pi i/4} = \sqrt{2} \cos \frac{11 \pi}{4} + i \sqrt{2} \sin \frac{11 \pi}{4} = \boxed{-1 + i}$.
